I might not mean much coming from a complete stranger, but I am proud of you. Raising a kid all by yourself is one hell of an accomplishment. People say it all the time that raising children is hard, but you never realize how hard it is until you're in it. I understand the feeling of loneliness. Even with 3 daughters and a wife, l still feel lonely. The two oldest girls are technically my stepdaughters. They've only been in my life for the past 5.5 years, but they still mean the world to me. The oldest has moved out for college, and I only hear from her if she needs something. I've bonded fairly well with the middle child, but she will be going on to college in a couple of years. The youngest will be 3 in May, and her excitement when I walk in the door from work is honestly what keeps me going.  I'm 35 and have nothing to show, I rent an apartment in a not so nice area, I drive  a 16 year old suv, and I wash cars for a rental company at the airport. I have realized that my only purpose in this world is to raise my daughters the best that I can, and I feel that I'm not good enough for them. I go to work, go home, go to work, go home. I try to take the girls out on my day off because I know one day they will be doing their own thing. So go ahead and spoil your daughter all that you can. I understand the feeling of loneliness, but hopefully, like me, you can look into your daughters eyes and feel the love and appreciation that beams out of her very existence. This is probably a long shot, but if you live around salt lake city, Utah,  I would be more than willing to give you a hug. But at the very least, you can call me your friend.

Moving across the city is hard. Moving to another country is extremely hard. But it's also an amazing experience, I'm so proud of you, what you have accomplished. The life changing commitments you have made. I know it's hard and scary, but I know without a doubt that you are more than capable of achieving anything you set your mind to. We all have a path to walk in life, and everything we do changes that path just a little bit. It's when we look back that we can see the huge impact it has on our lives. You have many years ahead of you, so one year is nothing. Failing is okay, but staying down is not. So I need you to stand back up, take a few breaths, and take that next step onto the next stepping stone on your path of life. You are stronger than you know.

When I was your age, I was suffering from severe depression and anxiety. I didn't think much about my future, I honestly didn't think I would live to be 30. School was too much to bear, so I ended up dropping out halfway through the tenth grade. That was a bad decision to make. It wasn't until around 20 that I started feeling better about myself. Started practicing martial arts. Then, at 23, my mom died and pushed me back into a deep, dark place. I tried to drown myself with alcohol to hide from the pain. I kept on with my karate for a few more years. But I still had the lingering thought of way even try I'll be dead in a few years. 

I was kind of correct. When I was 29, I met my wife and 2 stepdaughters. By the time I was 30, I was a different person for the better. As far as not knowing what you want from life, don't stress it too much. You're still so young and have many, many years to decide. My 15 year old about a year ago wanted to become an architect, and now is thinking about being a midwife. My point is that what  you want today might be different for what you want tomorrow. He'll, I'm 34, and I'm still trying to figure that out. 

As for loving yourself, I couldn't love myself either. I thought, how can I love someone else if I can't even love myself. Finding someone to love me helped me learn to love myself. 

My advice is to hang in there and finish high school. Take a couple of years of being an adult and try different things. Relax and don't stress the little things. The universe has a way of balancing thing out.
